extraction.name: MathVista
extraction.description: MATHVISTA is a benchmark for evaluating mathematical reasoning of foundation models in visual contexts. It consists of 6,141 examples derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA), covering diverse mathematical reasoning types, tasks, and visual contexts.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao
extraction.rai:dataCollection: MATHVISTA was compiled from 31 source datasets: 9 existing math-targeted multimodal datasets, 19 publicly available VQA datasets containing math-related instances, and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA). For VQA datasets, the authors reviewed more than 70 datasets and used heuristic rules to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning, then engaged three expert annotators to manually label whether the selected examples involved mathematical reasoning. For the three new datasets, questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields and refined through a rigorous review process. Each source dataset was limited to up to 400 examples to ensure balanced representation.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Document analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data come from 31 source datasets, including 9 existing MathQA datasets, 19 existing VQA datasets, and 3 newly annotated datasets. IQTest examples were sourced from puzzle test figures on online learning platforms; FunctionQA contains functional plot questions; PaperQA contains questions derived from academic illustrations including tables, figures, and charts from online education resources, with 107 examples sourced from papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: PaperQA examples were sourced from papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Each source dataset was limited to up to 400 examples to ensure balanced representation. For VQA datasets, heuristic rules selected examples with numeric answers or quantity words in the questions, followed by manual filtering using majority voting. For release, the dataset was split into testmini and test; testmini was sampled by first randomly sampling questions with a threshold number of 4 for each source dataset and then randomly sampling the remaining questions for each source dataset based on its proportion in the entire set.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For VQA datasets, the authors designed heuristic rules to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning from a large pool of candidates. Examples with numeric answers or containing quantity words in the questions were selected, yielding 4,949 VQA-format examples, after which false positives were removed through expert annotation. The authors also conducted several quality checks to address unidentified errors. For evaluation, answers are normalized to required answer formats.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Examples were annotated with metadata including question type, answer type, language, source, category, task, grade level, visual context, and required reasoning skills. Coarse labels of mathematical reasoning were automatically obtained from source dataset details. To verify automatic annotation quality, expert annotators manually labeled mathematical reasoning categories for 1,000 examples. For selecting math-related VQA examples, three expert annotators manually labeled whether examples involved mathematical reasoning. For the three new datasets, all questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields, and each dataset was independently annotated by three reviewers, with disagreements resolved through discussion among the review team.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A custom annotation tool/GUI developed by the authors
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For the newly collected 736 questions, each dataset was independently annotated by three reviewers, resulting in an inter-annotation consistency rate of 99.2%; only 6 questions exhibited disagreements, which were resolved through discussion. For human labeling of whether problems involved mathematical reasoning, the authors used Fleiss Kappa and reported 0.775, indicating substantial agreement. For mathematical reasoning category labels, 94.1% of examples from automatic and human annotations had the exact same set of reasoning types, and 98.79% of individual labels were identical.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Graduate students in STEM fields; three expert annotators; qualified human annotators for human baseline on Amazon Mechanical Turk with a high school diploma or higher, more than 5,000 HIT tasks completed, and acceptance score higher than 0.99
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Heuristic rules for automatic selection, GPT-4 answer extractor, EasyOCR
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The answer labels for the test split will not be publicly released to prevent data contamination, and the authors will maintain an online evaluation platform. The benchmark is described as part of an ongoing research process, and the authors are committed to maintaining the datasets, refining potential data noise in response to community feedback, and evolving the leaderboard in response to new models.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Language; grade level; educational attainment of human annotators
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to facilitate development of AI assistants capable of mathematical reasoning in visual contexts, with potential applications in education, statistical analysis, theorem proving, and scientific discovery. The paper states that MATHVISTA will play a critical role in the development of general-purpose AI agents capable of tackling mathematically intensive and visually rich real-world tasks.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that source annotations were sourced from original data providers, resulting in only 85.6% of examples having annotations, and that due to heterogeneity of sources, annotations lack a unified format and structure. It also notes possible gaps in representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals, and that the benchmark focuses on specific domains like science and college-level math.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The paper states several limitations: there may be gaps in representation of certain mathematical problems and visual contexts; the focus on mathematical reasoning in visual contexts across specific domains like science and college-level math makes high-quality data collection labor-intensive; scalability and generalizability to other domains remain a concern; only 85.6% of examples have annotations; annotations from original providers lack a unified format and structure; and the study focused exclusively on the most recent and prominent models.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is a benchmark for evaluating mathematical reasoning capabilities of foundation models in visual contexts. It is divided into testmini, intended for model development validation or for those with limited computing resources, and test, intended for standard evaluation. The test answer labels are not publicly released to prevent data contamination, and evaluation is intended through an online platform.
